state.misconception_label: Does not know the properties of a rectangle

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. The angle on the right hand side at the centre is highlighted in red and the angle at the bottom at the centre is highlighted in yellow.](). I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think all the angles in a rectangle are equal? Can you recall any properties of a rectangle that might help you determine the angles in this figure?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I thought that since it looks like a square, all the angles would be the same. But I know rectangles have right angles, right? So, does that mean the angles in the middle are also right angles? I'm still a bit confused about how the different lengths of the sides affect the angles.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you identify any other properties of a rectangle that might help you determine the angles at the center of the figure? How do the intersecting diagonals of a rectangle relate to the angles within the rectangle?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks valid questions about rectangle properties but doesn't directly address the student's confusion about why angles at the center differ from corner angles, and the student remains confused by Turn 2, showing minimal progress in understanding why the central angles formed by diagonals are not all equal in a non-square rectangle.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking about rectangle properties and diagonal relationships, never directly stating the answer, which is a textbook example of the Socratic method.
